centralVerdict: Failure, recovery, learning opportunity and mastery are distinct relations over evaluation scope, transition structure, evidence and SkillProfile. Failure has no intrinsic learning value; mastery has no intrinsic binary completion state.

reconstructions.from: FailureEvent as if a self-sufficient object state
reconstructions.to: FailureAssessment + authoritative failure signal when present
reconstructions.reason: the same history can satisfy one commitment and fail another; failure status requires evaluation scope/horizon/provenance
terminality depends on whether a recovery/continuation transition preserves the relevant pursuit identity within the declared horizon

reconstructions.from: LearningOpportunity as a property of failure
reconstructions.reason: learning potential depends on diagnosticity, actionability/controllability, re-exposure/recovery access, relevance and attribution; actual learning remains Human/System mechanism evidence

reconstructions.to: MasteryClaimSpec + SkillProfile evidence over declared probe/condition region
reconstructions.reason: mastery scope must state what robustness/generalization/retention/control claim is actually being made

reconstructions.to: local mastery claims with explicit scope
reconstructions.reason: continuous/open-ended practices can support bounded mastery claims without implying complete exhaustion of an unbounded skill space

objects.name: FailureAssessment
objects.definition: Evaluation/provenance-bound determination that a declared criterion/commitment was not satisfied within a declared scope/horizon. It may be local, attempt-scoped, run-scoped, match-scoped or practice-scoped.
objects.guard: FailureAssessment != ErrorEvent != Punishment != Loss != Death != Reset

objects.name: PursuitTerminalityClaim
objects.definition: Claim that, under the current pursuit identity and horizon, no authoritative continuation/recovery transition preserves pursuit of the same declared commitment.
objects.guard: terminality is scope/pursuit-relative; no retry button is not sufficient if another continuation path exists

objects.name: RecoveryTransitionSet
objects.definition: Authoritative transitions available after error/failure/setback, including next state, preserved/lost state, resource/history/time changes, eligibility and alternate pursuit paths.

objects.name: QuerySpecificRecoveryCostProjection
objects.definition: A declared weighted/partial projection of recovery transitions for a purpose such as time-to-retry, resource loss, information loss or participation interruption.
objects.guard: no universal weights without evaluation/PlayerValue semantics

objects.name: LearningOpportunityProfile
objects.definition: A structural/evidence-side profile of whether an episode exposes potentially learnable distinctions: relevant diagnostic signal, attributable/actionable correction, controllability, opportunity for re-exposure/probe, and sufficient preserved information/state for comparison.

objects.name: MasteryClaimSpec
objects.definition: Evidence contract for a mastery claim: attribution target, practice/evaluation scope, challenge/condition region, criterion, ProbeTransformation set, required robustness dimensions, history/retention horizon and identification status.
objects.guard: MasteryClaimSpec is a claim contract, not an ontology state called Mastered

objects.name: CapabilityMasteryClaim
objects.definition: Claim that the attribution target's SkillProfile satisfies the MasteryClaimSpec over the declared region with evidence strong enough for the stated identification status.
objects.guard: one demonstration/zero-error streak/high score does not establish it by identity

objects.name: DemonstratedMasteryEvidence
objects.definition: Observed performance episodes consistent with part or all of a MasteryClaimSpec under exact conditions.

learningOpportunityDimensions.name: Diagnosticity
learningOpportunityDimensions.question: Does the observation distinguish relevant hypotheses/errors/policy consequences rather than merely announce failure?

learningOpportunityDimensions.name: AttributionReliability
learningOpportunityDimensions.question: Can the target reasonably attribute the outcome to controllable/relevant action/state rather than opaque RNG/hidden causes?

learningOpportunityDimensions.name: Actionability
learningOpportunityDimensions.question: Does the evidence support a different candidate action/policy/attention allocation on a later probe?

learningOpportunityDimensions.name: Controllability
learningOpportunityDimensions.question: Can the attribution target influence the relevant variable at all?

learningOpportunityDimensions.name: ReExposureAccess
learningOpportunityDimensions.question: Can the distinction be tested again through retry/recovery/related future situations at an appropriate cost/horizon?

learningOpportunityDimensions.name: ComparabilityMemory
learningOpportunityDimensions.question: Are enough state/feedback/history distinctions preserved to compare the attempted and revised policy?

learningOpportunityDimensions.name: SRVSRelevance
learningOpportunityDimensions.question: Is the feedback about variables relevant to the current skill/evaluation claim rather than incidental telemetry?

masteryRobustnessDimensions: retention after declared delay where claimed
transfer across exact ProbeTransformations where claimed
recovery/control after errors or adverse states where claimed
independence from assistance where Human-independent mastery is claimed

matchedResults.result: a completed speedrun can be success for completion and failure for sub-40 criterion; failure is evaluation-relative
roguelike death can be run-level failure while meta-progression/knowledge commitment succeeds; death is not universal failure
same local failure signal is terminal under no continuation path and nonterminal under checkpoint/alternate recovery; failure status and terminality are separate
diagnostic controllable failures with cheap re-exposure score higher on structural learning-opportunity dimensions than opaque random failures with identical failure count
a saturated trivial task can yield zero failures while exposing no new skill-relevant distinction
structural learning opportunity can be present while a target's SkillProfile is held unchanged; opportunity != actual learning
two controllers can both satisfy nominal mastery criterion while only one satisfies retention/perturbation probes; nominal success != robust mastery
novice and expert can both show zero error on a saturated trivial challenge; zero errors do not identify mastery breadth
joint controller can satisfy a mastery criterion while Human-independent post-assist performance fails it; joint mastery evidence != Human-independent mastery
continuous expressive quality can support a bounded mastery claim over declared quality/control probes without terminal completion or claim of maximal possible skill
task-specific retained mastery can coexist with failed transfer to an untrained transformation; local mastery != general mastery
two recovery transitions trade time loss against resource/history loss; without weights no universal severity ordering exists

laws: GameOver signal != participation-level terminality by identity
Diagnosticity without Actionability/Controllability != sufficient learning opportunity
Cheap retry can increase re-exposure without making the challenge easy
High recovery cost can suppress re-exposure without increasing immediate skill challenge
Mastery does not require terminal completion or a globally maximal skill state

externalAnchors.pressure: mixed-methods game study with 182 participants supports goal-relative success/failure and temporary versus more enduring/perpetual failure distinctions
motor error feedback can act as a teaching signal and individual feedback responses correlate with learning; supports informative error mechanisms without making all failure educational
subjective error estimation interacted with extrinsic feedback frequency in children's motor learning; feedback structure matters beyond error occurrence
feedback after good versus poor trials produced different delayed learning despite similar practice performance; failure/error-focused feedback is not universally superior
productive-failure randomized studies found problem solving before instruction improved conceptual understanding/transfer; the mechanism includes subsequent instruction rather than failure alone
deliberate erring followed by correction can improve retention/far transfer in conceptual learning; correction/context are part of the intervention
30h directed video-game training produced durable task-specific gains without transfer to untrained tasks; trained mastery cannot imply broad transfer
overtraining basic laparoscopic skill did not improve retention and had limited transfer efficiency; overlearning/performance plateau does not establish general mastery
constant and faded feedback both improved acquisition, but faded feedback showed better delayed retention/transfer, reinforcing acquisition performance != durable mastery evidence
video-game expertise analysis warns that aggregate score obscures strategies/errors/representations supporting skilled performance; mastery evidence should not collapse to score

N0: error feedback can support motor learning but feedback organization matters; productive failure includes instruction/correction; task-specific training gains do not imply transfer; overtraining does not guarantee retention/generalization

foundationReopen.reason: D refines downstream evaluation, recovery, evidence and mastery claims over frozen SkillProfile/ProbeTransformation and existing authority/transition/evaluation coordinates; no frozen foundation contradiction appears.
